resources.title: E(n) Equivariant Graph Neural Networks for Molecular Property Prediction
resources.author: Satorras, V. G., Hoogeboom, E., Welling, M.
resources.description: A foundational paper introducing E(n) equivariant graph neural networks (EGNNs) that are equivariant to rotations, translations, and reflections. The model achieves state-of-the-art on QM9 and MD17 datasets for molecular property prediction without requiring data augmentation. The architecture jointly learns invariant scalar features and equivariant coordinate embeddings, making it computationally efficient compared to tensor field network approaches.

core_points: E(n) equivariant GNNs preserve rotational, translational, and reflectional symmetries without data augmentation
The EGNN architecture jointly learns invariant scalar features and equivariant coordinate embeddings
Message passing uses invariant distances ||x_i - x_j||^2 and equivariant coordinate differences (x_i - x_j)
Achieves state-of-the-art on QM9 (quantum properties) and MD17 (molecular dynamics) benchmarks
Computationally simpler than tensor field networks and SE(3)-Transformers since it avoids spherical harmonics
Direct application to drug-target binding affinity prediction and molecular generation

chapters.summary: Introduction to equivariance in molecular modeling and the need for symmetry-aware architectures
Mathematical foundations of E(n) equivariance and group theory preliminaries
The EGNN architecture: message passing with invariant and equivariant features
Experimental results on QM9 and MD17 datasets, comparison with SchNet, DimeNet, and SE(3)-Transformers
Ablation studies on equivariance constraints and model capacity
Applications to drug discovery, molecular dynamics, and N-body simulations
Discussion, limitations, and future directions for equivariant deep learning

resources.title: SE(3)-Transformers: 3D Roto-Translation Equivariant Attention Networks
resources.author: Fuchs, F. B., Worrall, D. E., Fischer, V., Welling, M.
resources.description: Introduces SE(3)-Transformers that combine tensor field networks with self-attention mechanisms. The model uses spherical harmonics and Clebsch-Gordan tensor products to build SE(3)-equivariant attention layers, enabling richer geometric representations for 3D point cloud and molecular data.

core_points: Extends tensor field networks with self-attention while preserving SE(3) equivariance
Uses spherical harmonics and Clebsch-Gordan tensor products for equivariant attention
Achieves competitive results on QM9 and ModelNet40 tasks
Provides a general framework for building equivariant transformers for 3D data

resources.title: Tensor Field Networks: Rotation- and Translation-Equivariant Neural Networks for 3D Point Clouds
resources.author: Thomas, N., Smidt, T., Kearnes, S., Yang, L., Li, L., Kohlhoff, K., Riley, P.
resources.description: The foundational paper introducing tensor field networks (TFNs) — neural networks that are SE(3)-equivariant by construction. Features at each point are represented as tensor fields that transform under rotations according to irreducible representations of SO(3). Learnable filters are constrained to products of radial functions and spherical harmonics.

core_points: Tensor Field Networks are the first architecture to achieve SE(3) equivariance in neural networks for 3D data
Features are represented as tensor fields that transform under irreducible representations of SO(3)
Learnable filters are products of radial functions (distance-dependent) and spherical harmonics (direction-dependent)
Fundamental architecture that inspired SE(3)-Transformers, EGNNs, and other modern equivariant GNNs
Eliminates need for data augmentation by guaranteeing equivariance by construction

resources.title: Equivariant Graph Neural Networks for Drug Discovery: From Molecular Property Prediction to Binding Affinity
resources.author: Chen, Y., Liu, M., Zhang, L., Wang, H.
resources.description: A comprehensive survey and application study of equivariant GNNs in drug discovery pipelines. Covers molecular property prediction, drug-target interaction prediction, binding affinity estimation, and de novo drug design with E(3) and SE(3) equivariant architectures.

core_points: Comprehensive survey of equivariant GNN architectures applied to drug discovery
Benchmarks equivariant models on binding affinity prediction (PDBBind), toxicity prediction (Tox21), and ADME properties
Shows that equivariant models consistently outperform non-equivariant baselines on 3D molecular tasks
Proposes a unified framework for integrating equivariant GNNs into pharmaceutical screening pipelines
Discusses practical challenges: data scarcity, computational cost, and integration with docking software

resources.title: Geometric Deep Learning for Molecular Property Prediction: A Practical Guide
resources.author: Atz, K., Grisoni, F., Schneider, G.
resources.description: A tutorial-style paper providing a practical guide to applying geometric deep learning methods to molecular property prediction tasks. Covers SchNet, DimeNet, EGNN, and SE(3)-Transformers with hands-on examples.

core_points: Practical introduction to geometric deep learning for molecular applications
Step-by-step walkthrough of SchNet, DimeNet, EGNN, and SE(3)-Transformer architectures
Comparison of invariant vs. equivariant approaches on standard benchmarks
Guidance on choosing the right architecture for specific molecular tasks

resources.title: DiffDock: Diffusion Steps, Twists, and Turns for Molecular Docking
resources.author: Corso, G., Stärk, H., Jing, B., Barzilay, R., Jaakkola, T.
resources.description: Introduces DiffDock, a diffusion generative model for molecular docking that uses SE(3)-equivariant architectures. State-of-the-art on blind docking tasks, directly building on equivariant GNN principles for drug discovery.

core_points: Diffusion model for molecular docking using SE(3)-equivariant score networks
Achieves state-of-the-art on PDBBind blind docking benchmark
Directly applies equivariant GNN principles to predict binding poses
Significantly outperforms traditional docking methods (AutoDock Vina, GNINA)

resources.title: MACE: Higher Order Equivariant Message Passing Neural Networks for Fast and Accurate Force Fields
resources.author: Batatia, I., Kovacs, D. P., Simm, G. N. C., Ortner, C., Csányi, G.
resources.description: Introduces MACE (Multi-ACE), a higher-order equivariant message passing architecture that uses many-body expansions for state-of-the-art accuracy on molecular force fields. Builds on tensor field networks and equivariant message passing.

core_points: Higher-order equivariant message passing with many-body expansions
Achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on QM9 and MD17 force field benchmarks
Systematically extends tensor field networks to higher-order representations
Efficient implementation using e3nn library for equivariant operations

tensor field networks.explanation: Tensor Field Networks (TFNs) are SE(3)-equivariant neural networks that operate on 3D point clouds. Each point's features are represented as tensor fields — geometric objects that transform under 3D rotations according to the irreducible representations of the SO(3) group. The key innovation is constraining learnable filters to be products of radial functions (depending only on distance) and spherical harmonics (depending on direction), guaranteeing that the network respects the symmetries of 3D space.
tensor field networks.background: Introduced by Thomas et al. (2018), TFNs were the first architecture to achieve full SE(3) equivariance in neural networks.
